body.p: The following is intended as a full and complete response to the non-final Office action dated October 21, 2024. In this response, claims 41-45, 47, 51, 53, 56-63, 67-69, and 72-79 are amended. Claims 48-50, 54-55, 64-66, 70-71, and 80 are cancelled. No new matter is added by way of these amendments. Favorable reconsideration is requested for the reasons presented below.
Applicant thanks the Examiner for confirming that the IDSs filed on July 27, 2023 and April 1, 2024, and references cited therein, have been considered.
Applicant kindly requests the Examiner to consider the references cited in the IDS filed on November 16, 2024 in the next Office communication.

The Office action objected to claims 53 and 69 for containing informalities. The claims are amended herein to address the informalities by removing the extraneous "and" at the end of claims 53 and 69. No new matter is added.
Withdrawal of the claim objections is respectfully requested.
Rejections under QQ 102, 103 and Allowable Subject Matter

The Office action rejected claims 41, 46-53, 56-57, 62-69, 72-73, and 78-80 under 35 U.S.C. §102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Matsumura (US 2017/0297567). Claims 42-43, 58- 59, and 74-75 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Matsumura in view of Woon (US 2020/0346643). Claims 44, 60, and 76 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Matsumura in view of Woon and Park (US 2016/0096430). Claims 45, 61, and 77 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §103 as being unpatentable over Matsumura in view of Park.

In addition, the Office action indicated that claims 54-55 and 70-71 include allowable subject matter and would be allowable if rewritten in independent form to include all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims.

In this response, without necessarily agreeing with the substance of the rejections, independent claims 41 and 57 are amended to incorporate the features of allowable dependent claims 54 and 70, respectively. Claims 41 and 57 are therefore believed to be allowable. In
addition, independent claim 73 is also amended to recite similar features. Claim 73 is therefore believed to be allowable for at least the same reasons as claims 41 and 57.
The remaining claims depend from one of allowable claims 41, 57 or 73, and are therefore also believed to be allowable.

In view of the foregoing remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that the patent application is in condition for allowance. If, in the opinion of the Examiner, a telephone conference would expedite the prosecution of the subject application, the Examiner is invited to call the undersigned attorney.
SVG {EMBED HERE} 0.4271.383 Arthur J. Bobel, Reg. No. 69,031
